question: At the first position where the served (hand_weight 0.9) and blind (0.0) arms choose different moves, does a hand-blind deeper oracle prefer the served move, and does that preference separate config-decided pairs from divergent splits?
why_now: The 2026-10-18 d2 reason tally showed every decisive game ends at a root mate-in-1, so terminal tactical access is not the mechanism; pair divergence starts at ply 0-4. The remaining question is whether the coefficient's early divergences are quality improvements or arbitrary perturbations.
consumer: The decision whether further hand-policy work should target evaluation quality (the term carries positional information) or should be treated as a perturbation whose outcome effects are incidental; no product or default change follows from this bounded result either way.

inputs.positions: one shared position per colour-swapped pair: the first ply index where the two saved move lists differ

groups.config_decided: pairs where the served-configured side won both colours (2) or lost both colours (0)
groups.divergent_split: pairs where the move lists differ but the same colour won both games

method.position_reconstruction: replay the first game's saved moves through the shipped root search with that game's arm config, asserting each chosen action's text equals the saved move; both games share this prefix
method.candidate_moves: regenerate both arms' root choices at the shared position with their own configs and assert they equal the saved moves
method.oracle: apply each candidate move, then run a fresh hand-blind (hand_weight 0.0) depth-4, 20000-node, quiescence 4/hard 8, ordering-on, TT-off root search from the resulting state; value = negative of the returned score so it is expressed for the mover at the shared position
method.search_budget_per_position: 2 reconstruction-side searches for candidates + 2 oracle searches plus the replay prefix

guards.no_overwrite: refuses to write an existing result path
guards.abort_behaviour: on guard trip, write the partial file with an explicit interrupted flag and no aggregate claim

endpoint.primary: counts of served-better / blind-better / tie judged deltas in the config-decided group
endpoint.secondary: same counts in the divergent-split group
endpoint.prewritten_tie_break: only for positions whose depth-4 oracle gives an exact tie, and only if at most 60 searches and 600 s remain of the budget already declared above: re-judge the same pair with hand_weight 0.0 at depth 6 and 40000 nodes, and report both the depth-4 and the depth-6 sign so the depth-4 tie count is not silently upgraded to a preference
endpoint.reported_quantities: per-position delta, both oracle scores, oracle node/qnode totals and termination reasons, tie threshold equals exact score equality
endpoint.no_p_values: Designed as a descriptive quality check on already-observed positions; no hypothesis test, no endpoint tuning.

done_condition: result file written with all reachable positions (or explicit per-position failures), reader reproduces the aggregate, README/claim updated, no product code touched
limitations_prewritten: a depth-4 hand-blind search is a stronger judge but not ground truth; it shares the shipped evaluation except the hand term
the depth-6 tie-break is a second fixed judge at a different budget, not ground truth, and is applied only to depth-4 exact ties so it cannot select the depth-4 endpoint
4x4 generated seeds with one start each; positions are only where the two arms diverged
ties and quantisation can make equal scores hide different play
no strength, distribution or generality claim; no independent rerun by another role
